newsitem.title: USA: IBM to release results after market close Jan. 21.
newsitem.headline: IBM to release results after market close Jan. 21.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp., in a major change, will release its fourth-quarter earnings after the stock market closes on Tuesday, Jan. 21, analysts said Monday.
The computer giant, based in Armonk, N.Y., for years has released its earnings before the stock market opened.

But analysts said they did not believe the change has any negative implications for the quarter and said that IBM was making the change to avoid the wild swings in its stock that have occurred as it held conference calls with Wall Street analysts following such announcements.
The conference calls will continue to be held sometime after earnings are released.

"I don't think it's relative to their quarterly performance," said Gary Helmig, a SoundView Financial analyst. "What was happening is that they would release the numbers and they would have people in and out of the stock while the meeting was going on. They decided it made a lot more sense to do this when the market wasn't trading."
Many technology companies, especially those on the West Coast, release their earnings after the stock market closes.
An IBM spokesman said the company recently conducted an internal review of its entire earnings process, which included discussions with members of the investment community.

"Many members told us they would like us to release earnings after the close," said an IBM spokesman. "So it's a combination of internal review and comments from the investment community." He declined to comment about the volatility of IBM's stock on earnings days and whether this was a factor in IBM's decision.
"Many technology companies release their earnings after the close," the spokesman said.
IBM said it will decide whether to stick to the new timing for earnings releases after it receives feedback from Wall Street analysts.

"It's a new year and they are trying to change their format to reflect a less chaotic environment where they are talking to the investment community while their stock is being traded," said John Jones, a Salomon Brothers analyst.
"I think they are going to have a better quarter than expected," he said.
Jones said he expects "modest earnings above consensus," of around $3.90 to $4.00 a share, for the fourth quarter.
IBM reported net operating profits of $1.29 billion, or $2.45 cents a share, on revenues of $18.1 billion in the third quarter.
IBM's stock rose $2 to $161.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
